wins.text: Q1 total revenue hit a record $19.3B, up 29% YoY, exceeding guidance driven by better-than-expected AI semiconductor growth
AI semiconductor revenue grew 106% YoY to $8.4B in Q1, well above outlook; Q2 guided to $10.7B, up ~140% YoY
Q1 adjusted EBITDA reached a record $13.1B (68% of revenue), above guidance of 67%, with semiconductor operating margin up 260 bps YoY to 60%
Returned $10.9B to shareholders in Q1 via $7.8B in buybacks (~23M shares) and $3.1B in dividends; Board authorized additional $10B repurchase program through end of CY2026
Announced sixth XPU customer (OpenAI) deploying first-gen XPU in 2027 at over 1 gigawatt; line of sight to AI chip revenue in excess of $100B in 2027 with supply chain secured through 2028

risks.text: Non-GAAP tax rate for Q2 FY2026 guided to ~16.5%, up from FY25 levels, due to global minimum tax and geographic income mix shift — a headwind to EPS
Infrastructure Software revenue grew only 1% YoY in Q1, reflecting slower near-term growth as VMware transition matures; Q2 guided to 9% YoY, still well below semiconductor growth rates
Inventory days on hand rose to 68 days in Q1 from 58 days in Q4 as Broadcom pre-builds to secure AI supply — execution risk if demand timing shifts
Concentration risk: AI revenue is heavily dependent on just 6 hyperscaler/LLM customers, each of whom is also investing in internal COT (customer-owned tooling) chip programs
Constrained leading-edge wafer, HBM, and substrate capacity across the industry creates supply chain risk, though Broadcom claims to have secured capacity through 2028

guidance_items.detail: Q2 FY2026 consolidated revenue guided to ~$22B, up 47% YoY — a sharp acceleration from Q1's 29% YoY growth
Q2 semiconductor revenue guided to ~$14.8B, up 76% YoY; AI semiconductor specifically guided to $10.7B, up ~140% YoY
Q2 Infrastructure Software revenue guided to ~$7.2B, up 9% YoY vs. 1% YoY in Q1
Q2 consolidated gross margin expected flat sequentially at 77%; adjusted EBITDA guided to ~68% of revenue
Management provided 2027 AI chip revenue visibility 'in excess of $100B', with ~10 gigawatts of XPU shipments anticipated across 6 customers

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Gross margin dilution risk from rack-level system shipments (vs. chip-only sales)
Customer-owned tooling (COT) competitive threat from hyperscalers building in-house XPUs
Disaggregation of prefill/decode workloads and its impact on GPU vs. custom silicon demand mix
